claims.text: A controlled high-temperature pre-oxidation treatment will improve the RHEA's oxygen resistance during subsequent extreme-temperature exposure.
The pre-oxidation treatment will form a continuous, adherent, CrTaO4-rich surface oxide layer.
The untreated RHEA forms a non-protective oxide scale during high-temperature exposure.
The untreated RHEA's oxide scale grows rapidly during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The intervention is a single-step pre-oxidation treatment under oxygen-limited conditions.
Pre-oxidation at about 1100°C under low oxygen partial pressure for 1–2 hours is proposed.
The proposed service exposure is 1200°C in air for 100 hours.
The resulting structural mediator is a dense CrTaO4-rich oxide scale.
The pre-established CrTaO4-rich layer acts as a diffusion barrier.
The CrTaO4-rich layer reduces inward oxygen transport during extreme-temperature exposure.
Reduced inward oxygen transport minimizes further oxidation of the underlying alloy.
Minimizing oxidation preserves the alloy's structural integrity.
Relative to untreated samples, pre-oxidized samples will have lower weight gain after 100 hours at 1200°C in air.
Relative to untreated samples, pre-oxidized samples will exhibit slower oxide-scale growth after 100 hours at 1200°C in air.
Reduced weight gain and slower scale growth indicate enhanced high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The expected improvement is limited to the specified pre-oxidation and service-exposure conditions.
Performance outside the specified processing and exposure conditions is uncertain.
The optimal pre-oxidation temperature, duration, and oxygen partial pressure remain to be determined.
The effectiveness of the proposed CrTaO4 scale across slight alloy-composition variations remains unverified.
